summary: Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts as assistant professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013-2014) at Ryukoku University.

Masaaki Sugiyama (1952-2019) worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970-1979) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1982 to 1989.
Masaaki Tsuchiya (born 1960) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979-1989) and held a position at Senshu University around 2003.

Masaharu Anesaki (1873-1949) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University, he served as a professor (from 1904) and library director (1923-1934) at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai (born 1942), a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology, completed his doctorate at Tokyo University of Education (~1961-1977). He held positions at Ibaraki University and the University of Tsukuba, becoming professor emeritus in 2006.

Masahide Mori (born 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later serving as assistant professor and professor at Kanazawa University from circa 1997.
Masahide Tsujimura specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Kyoto University and served as an assistant professor at Kobe University in 2013.
Masahiro Asada (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1964 to 1973 and served there as an assistant professor from circa 1983 to 1990.

Masahiro Inami (born 1960) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (~1985-1990) and held teaching appointments at Tokyo Gakugei University from circa 1995 to 2009.

Masahiro Kusunoki (1921-2009) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1947-1953), he served as professor of religious studies and history of religion there from circa 1974 to 1984.

Masahiro Shimoda (born 1957) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo Metropolitan University, and the University of Tsukuba, he served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1994-2023) and Musashino University (2023).
Masahiro Takano (born 1960) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a librarian in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita (born 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1968-1978), where he later served as head of the Department of the History of Japanese Philosophy from circa 2001 to 2014.

Masakazu Tanaka (born 1955) works in religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics, later serving as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988-2019) and vice president at PIF (2019).

Masako Keta (born 1953) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied under Yoshinori Takeuchi at Kyoto University. She served as an assistant professor and professor at Kanazawa University, then professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000-2018).
Masamichi Asukai (1934-2000) was a scholar of Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1953 to 1957 and held an academic post there from circa 1969 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo (born 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao at Otani and Kyoto universities, holding professorships at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna, where he was supervised by Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served at Chikushi Jogakuen University as a lecturer (attested 1991) and as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 2002).

Masanori Shono works in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).
